title: SCIM observability-driven adaptive retry playbook for cross-tenant deprovisioning
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Background: We continue to see sporadic customer reports where SCIM deprovisioning either stalls or results in inconsistent group membership across downstream services. Current retry logic is a flat exponential backoff with little signal about error causality or tenant priority, which makes debugging and customer-level SLAs unreliable.

Goal: Implement an observability-first, adaptive retry playbook for SCIM user/group deprovision flows that: 1) classifies errors into transient vs. semantic/conflict categories, 2) surfaces causal trace IDs across SCIM request -> audit log -> job queue for root-cause analysis, and 3) establishes per-tenant prioritized retry tiers and staged deprovision semantics (suspend -> tombstone -> delete) to reduce orphaned membership and customer impact.

Success metrics:
- Reduce customer-facing deprovision incidents by 65% within 4 weeks of rollout.
- P95 time-to-final-deprovision under normal load decreases or remains stable.
- Mean MTTR for SCIM-deprov incidents decreases from 3.8h to <1.5h via causal traces and dashboards.

Design summary:
1) Error classification middleware: enrich SCIM responses with classification tags: TRANSIENT_NETWORK, RATE_LIMIT, CONFLICT_SEMANTIC, AUTH_FAILURE, OTHER. Classification rules and examples documented in Confluence.
2) Adaptive retry tiers:
   - Tier A (high-priority tenants with reserved capacity): immediate low-latency retry with limited exponential backoff + jitter, higher quota.
   - Tier B (standard tenants): backoff windows that scale with tenant error rate and traffic (adaptive window).
   - Tier C (bulk or third-party syncs): longer windows and batched reconciliation.
3) Staged deprovision lifecycle: SUSPENDED (30d TTL) -> TOMBSTONE (extendable) -> DELETE. If membership reconciliation fails during SUSPENDED, escalate to human review queue with causal trace included.
4) Causal tracing: assign scim_cause_id per SCIM change request, propagate into audit logs, job queue messages, and HTTP response headers. This id surfaces in Console trace views and the new SCIM incident dashboard.
5) Observability: add metrics and logs: scim.deprov.retry.count, scim.deprov.retry.window_seconds, scim.deprov.finalize.latency_p90, scim.deprov.causal_traces, scim.deprov.orphaned_members_total. Dashboards and alerting thresholds defined in the design doc.
6) Safe defaults and rollouts: feature-flagged rollout per-tenant with canary group of 10 tenants, monitor for false positives in classification, and automatic rollback if orphaned members spike >15% vs baseline.

Acceptance criteria:
- Middleware classification adds scim_error_class tag to >99% of SCIM responses in canary.
- Causal trace id is present in audit events and job messages and links to Console trace view.
- Retry queues respect per-tenant tiering and preserve order for group membership changes.
- Runbook updated and on-call engineer can run manual reconciliation with provided tooling.

Rollback plan:
- Immediately flip feature flag to previous behavior.
- Drain adaptive retry queues and revert queue schema changes.
- Re-run reconciliation for canary tenants and escalate incidents.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IDENTITY/SCIM+Adaptive+Retry+Playbook
- Runbook: https://runbook.redwood.ai/scim-deprov-runbook
- GitHub implementation PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5863 (middleware + metrics), https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5892 (queueing + staged lifecycle)
- Dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/SCIM/adaptive-retries

Implementation notes:
- Prefer idempotent operations and strong idempotency keys for user/group mutations to avoid double-deletes.
- We will introduce a lightweight channel between the SCIM gateway and the reconciliation worker that carries scim_cause_id and error_class.
- For group membership conflicts (409), we add a conflict resolution policy: retry once with conflict-backoff, then escalate to a compare-and-merge reconciliation job that attempts deterministic resolution and emits an audit event for human review.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Increased storage of tombstone state introduces retention costs; mitigated by TTL and tiered retention.
- Misclassification could delay necessary immediate deletes; mitigated via canary and metrics.
- Additional latency for high-volume tenants if adaptive backoff is too conservative; mitigated by Tier A reserved capacity option.

Notes for QA:
- QA harness should simulate: transient network failures, rate-limit bursts, 409 conflicts from concurrent updates, and long-running reconciliation failure.
- Validate causal_trace propagation across services and visibility in Console traces.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy middleware + metrics behind FF to staging.
2) Canary rollout to 10 tenants (Tier A and Tier B mix) for 7 days.
3) Monitor metrics and manual spot checks.
4) Incremental ramp to 25%, 50%, 100% with automated health gates.
